title: Srikant Tiwari Isn't Done Yet — Raj & DK Confirm They're 'Writing Furiously' on The Family Man Season 4
excerpt: The creators reveal that Seasons 3 and 4 were always planned as one continuous story, and the man who writes India's most agonizing fictional father is about to become one himself
body:
Seven months. That's how long fans of **The Family Man** have been staring at a black screen after Season 3's gut-wrenching cliffhanger, wondering whether Srikant Tiwari made it out alive. Now, they finally have their answer — or at least, the promise of one.

In a new interview with **Variety India**, creator **Raj Nidimoru** — one half of the filmmaking duo Raj & DK — confirmed that Season 4 is not just happening, it's already being written at a pace he describes as "furious."

> "We had always planned Seasons 3 and 4 as one long story. Some viewers felt Season 3 ended midway, but in our view the central narrative had reached a logical point. Only Srikant Tiwari's journey remained unfinished because it naturally continued into the next season. So yes, we're writing furiously. We have to get to the second part of that story." — Raj Nidimoru

That word — *midway* — is doing a lot of work here. What Raj is saying, plainly, is that Season 3 was never meant to stand alone. It was always the first half of a two-part story, a deliberate creative gamble that left audiences gasping but was never going to leave them stranded. Season 4 is the payoff.

## The Season That Broke Records — Then Broke Hearts

When **The Family Man Season 3** premiered on **Amazon Prime Video** in late 2025, it did what every previous season had done, only bigger. The show landed in the **Top 5 across 35+ countries** during its launch week, making it Prime Video's most-watched Indian series of the year. **Manoj Bajpayee**'s Srikant Tiwari — the middle-class intelligence officer who saves the nation between school runs and marital arguments — had become one of the most beloved characters in Indian streaming history.

But then came that ending. Season 3 plunged Srikant into the fraught world of **Northeast India's separatist politics** through a fictional government initiative called **Project Sahakar**. **Jaideep Ahlawat** arrived as **Rukma**, a quietly terrifying antagonist who assassinated local leaders and forced the government into crisis mode. **Nimrat Kaur** played Meera, adding layers of moral ambiguity that made the season's politics feel dangerously personal. And in a move that sent fan theories spiraling, the season also wove in a crossover with **Vijay Sethupathi**'s character from **Farzi**, Raj & DK's other Prime Video hit — suggesting a shared universe that's only getting started.

Then the screen went black. Srikant's fate was left hanging. And millions of viewers, from Mumbai to Manhattan, collectively lost their minds.

## Bajpayee Broke the Silence First

The actor hadn't waited for the creators to make it official. Within hours of Season 3's finale dropping, **Manoj Bajpayee** responded to a distraught fan on X with a reply that has since been screenshotted approximately four billion times:

> "Sabka jawab 4th season me hoga! Jaldi milte ha!" — (All answers will come in Season 4! See you soon!)

That was November 2025. By December, DK had hinted that the gap between seasons would be "sooner than later" — a significant promise, given that fans had waited nearly four years between Seasons 2 and 3.

## When Will It Actually Drop?

Here's what matters. If Raj & DK are writing "furiously" right now, when does the camera roll? Industry reports from earlier this year suggested filming could begin around **mid-2026** — which is, well, right about now. Given the show's intensive post-production requirements and Prime Video's scheduling preferences, a **late 2026 or early 2027** premiere looks realistic.

For diaspora audiences, the logistics are beautifully simple: **The Family Man** streams exclusively on **Amazon Prime Video**, which means it drops simultaneously across the US, UK, Canada, and everywhere else the moment it premieres. No VPN gymnastics. No waiting for a satellite window. Just Srikant, your couch, and whatever snack you were stress-eating during the Season 3 finale.

## The Off-Screen Plot Twist

Meanwhile, Raj Nidimoru is living through something that feels almost like a **Family Man** subplot. He married **Samantha Ruth Prabhu** — who, you'll remember, played the show's most electrifying antagonist, Raji, in Season 2 — in an intimate ceremony at the Isha Yoga Center in December 2025. And just last week, Samantha confirmed that she's **expecting their first child**, due later this year.

So the man who has spent four seasons writing about a spy who can't show up to his daughter's school function is about to become a father himself. If that doesn't sharpen the domestic-chaos scenes, nothing will.

**The Family Man** Seasons 1-3 are streaming now on **Amazon Prime Video**.
